# eala energy

> eala energy builds distributed AI compute infrastructure at structurally constrained renewable nodes of the UK grid.

eala energy captures clean power that today is curtailed and converts it into reliable compute, with an embedded energy-resilience layer for operational continuity and grid support. The platform combines containerised AI compute, an energy-resilience layer sized for long curtailment events, and a proprietary orchestration layer that continuously decides whether value is highest in compute, energy resilience, or grid services. Sites follow a 3–10 MW modular design with a 6–8 hr on-site energy-continuity layer.

Legal entity: EALA ENERGY LTD, registered in England and Wales, Companies House company number 17110070. Registered office: Rex House, 4-12 Regent Street, London, England, SW1Y 4PE.

## Insights

- [All insights](https://eala.energy/blog/): Insights from eala energy on distributed AI compute, curtailed renewable power and the energy-resilience layer.
- [Why long money doesn’t go where the curtailment is](https://eala.energy/blog/why-long-money-avoids-curtailment/): Behind the Scottish constraint, a battery may have three to five strong years; lenders want seven to ten. What kind of project fits that window?
- [How many hours can Britain’s batteries actually store?](https://eala.energy/blog/how-many-hours-can-britain-store/): Britain’s 8.7 GW battery fleet holds 14.1 GWh, about an hour and a half at full output. Why storage duration, and a load at the node, matter.
- [Is the battery party over?](https://eala.energy/blog/is-the-battery-party-over/): GB battery revenues hit £99k/MW a year in September, yet Norway’s oil fund says values are falling. Location, not chemistry, decided who won.
- [Are we using the batteries we already have?](https://eala.energy/blog/give-the-battery-a-job/): This summer batteries offered the grid twice as much energy as last year; under 6% was dispatched. The case for giving storage a job of its own.
- [Capital isn’t scarce. A place on the wires is.](https://eala.energy/blog/a-place-on-the-wires/): €270m for 350 MW at Kilmarnock South, and Ofgem plans a fee to hold a connection queue place. What’s scarce now is grid access, not capital.
- [Stop waiting for a socket](https://eala.energy/blog/stop-waiting-for-a-socket/): 90 GW of batteries built or queued against 29 GW needed by 2035, and soon a fee to stay in line. Why storage and compute behind a wind farm can build now.
